46f217c02a484ae652c43d874ab751e32bb2eaff.summary: Wiz reports on JINX-0164, a financially motivated actor active since at least mid-2025 that targets cryptocurrency-industry developers with fake recruiter and meeting lures. A two-week intrusion used a macOS infostealer, AUDIOFIX, to steal credentials, then injected it into internal code repositories. A trojanized npm SDK on April 7, 2026 delivered a second backdoor, MINIRAT. Wiz does not link the group to a sponsor. Similarities to North Korean groups are noted but not confirmed.

The GitHub source code was not modified, suggesting the attackers only had access to npm credentials.

hedges: The report says its themes are not exhaustive of all actors and means and presents only some prominent themes.
GTIG cannot confirm the potential validity of all the disseminated documents; the sensitive nature of some appears overstated.
Robust hacktivist activity can complicate attribution of state-backed actors that use hacktivist tactics.
GTIG assesses with low confidence that the UNC6508 actors likely sought to fulfill intelligence collection requirements; the intended focus is unknown.
Several China-nexus actors are described as suspected, including UNC5221, which the report says it suspects conducted the BRICKSTORM campaign.
The link between TEMP.Vermin and Luhansk People's Republic security agencies is one that CERT-UA has linked, as reported.
The report says Russian targeting of individuals is likely due at least in part to reliance on public and off-the-shelf technology.
The CANFAIL lure is described as appearing LLM-generated based on analysis, not as confirmed.
